claim: Palantir Technologies was seeded by In-Q-Tel, the CIA's venture-capital arm, which made two rounds of investment totaling more than $2 million in the young company — the only outside money it took for years. From 2005 to 2008 the CIA was Palantir's sole customer, alpha-testing and refining its data-analysis software before the company expanded to other agencies and commercial clients. Palantir was co-founded in 2003–2004 by PayPal veterans Peter Thiel and Alex Karp; its early product work drew on the same intelligence data-fusion problem that Total Information Awareness (TIA) had been built to solve. Not long after Palantir launched, Karp and Thiel met John Poindexter — the admiral who had directed TIA — at the home of former Defense Policy Board chair Richard Perle; by Karp's own account Poindexter was one of many experts the founders consulted early on. What the record does not support is the further claim that Poindexter connected the founders to the CIA: the canonical origin accounts credit the In-Q-Tel investment to a referral, not to Poindexter.
